3. Application stands disposed of.

6. Issue notice.
Mr. Satish Kumar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.

7. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr.Satpal Malik and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Kulbir Singh from Police Station Hari Nagar, Delhi.
8.
Brief facts of the present case are that petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 got married on 17.01.2019 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
No child was born out of the said wedlock.
It is stated that on 20.12.2018, respondent no. 2 had lodged an FIR bearing no. 564/2019 for offence punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 against the petitioners.

Thereafter, during pendency of the case, both the parties had amicably settled their disputes before the Counselling Cell, Family Court, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi on 20.05.2022 and had dissolved their marriage.

entities.text: Counselling Cell, Family Court, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 9. On a query made by this Court, the respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will, volition and without any coercion, pressure or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties before the Counselling Cell, Family Court, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi on 20.05.2022 and had dissolved their marriage by mutual consent.

entities.label: COURT

It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner no.1 and other family members.

11. As per settlement, petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs. 4,40,000/- to respondent no. 2 in three instalments in the following manner:
a. First installment of Rs.1,50,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording of statements in First motion.
b. Second installment of Rs.1,40,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording of statements in Second motion.
c. Third/Final instalment of Rs.1,50,000/- to be paid at the time of quashing of the FIR before the Hon'ble High Court at New Delhi.
12.

Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs. 1,50,000/- today, i.e., 15.09.2023 vide DD No. 417489 drawn on State Bank of Arun Sethi & Ors vs State Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156112300/

sentences.text: 2 India and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

13. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the above mentioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

14. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 564/2019, registered at Police Station Hari Nagar, New Delhi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
